prize_parts.citation: For introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and for showing how reallocation across firms shapes exporting, foreign investment and the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1. It is a single part, B038, with Melitz and Helpman. The change came earlier, when I moved my first choice from B001 to B038, and nothing in the round-1 exchange reverses it. I weigh three things. First, the conceptual step. Melitz (2003), together with Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) on exporting versus foreign investment, changed the unit of analysis in trade from countries and industries to heterogeneous firms. That produced a selection channel and a reallocation channel for gains from trade that the earlier frameworks did not have. Second, maturity. More than twenty years of use on customs and production microdata, plus extension into macro, industrial organisation and development, give an evidence base that is much longer than B001's. Third, exact credit. A two-name set tracks the core model (Melitz) and the architect of the broader firm-level agenda (Helpman). I would word the citation around the mechanism of selection and reallocation and not around any welfare magnitude, because the qualitative result is better supported than the quantitative one. The chair asked whether one standard can be applied to B038 and B015. I think it can. For each candidate I ask whether the credited discovery is a distinct conceptual step beyond earlier prizes, whether it has been tested against data, and whether three names can describe it without misdescribing how the field was built. On the first test, I read the 2008 trade prize (trade patterns and location under increasing returns) as separable from firm selection. I read earlier macroeconomics prizes on expectations, time consistency and policy rules as separable from nominal rigidity and staggered pricing. Neither overlap question clearly separates the two. On the second test, the two candidates differ. B038's central mechanism has been tested directly on firm-level data, while B015's building blocks (Calvo pricing, Taylor contracts) have a more mixed micro record, as Friberg notes. The third test separates them most. I therefore keep B038 first, and I keep B015 and B001 as alternatives, not as parts.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have serious claims on closely related firm-level trade work, and Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are real. A Melitz-Helpman prize could be read as under-crediting the empirical exporter facts and the quantitative strand. The chair asked what separates the founding contribution from those empirical facts. My answer is that the exporter-premium facts were documented first, and the model supplied the selection and reallocation mechanism that explained them and generated new testable predictions. That is a judgement about which contribution is the discovery, not something the evidence settles. I also accept that gains-from-trade magnitudes are sensitive to elasticity and functional-form assumptions. If the committee thinks the empirical firm-level literature is inseparable from the model, then a two-name set is the wrong shape, and I could not defend it on scientific grounds alone. A further point is my own possible bias. I gave the 2020 presentation speech, which emphasised work that 'brought theory to practice'. That speech was not a statement of my preferences, but I may overweight candidates whose empirical use is easy to show.

responses.point: Hassler defends B015 as the strongest combination of conceptual change, durability and practical consequence. He values the origins-plus-synthesis trio of Taylor, Calvo and Woodford, and he accepts that excluding Galí and Gertler is a real cost, not a technicality.
responses.response: I accept that B015 is more influential on policy practice than B038 is on trade policy, and I do not dispute its maturity. The disagreement is about whether influence settles the prize design. You frame the trio as the origins of the building blocks plus the synthesis. That is a coherent reading, but it is also a choice that sets aside the canonical model and the estimation work of Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, and you describe that as a real cost. Friberg's point also applies here: the survival of a workhorse framework through 2008 and 2021-23 shows it is adaptable, which is weaker evidence that Calvo pricing and Taylor contracts specifically were confirmed. If the committee settled the citation and resolved the attribution, I would take B015 very seriously, so I keep it as my first alternative. As it stands, B038 has the smaller attribution problem, and I apply the same distinctness test to the 2008 trade prize and to the earlier macroeconomics prizes.

responses.point: Enflo defends B038 and keeps Redding out so the citation stays focused. She treats the welfare-gain numbers as a limit and says the qualitative result that selection and reallocation matter is much better supported than any single magnitude.
responses.response: I agree, and the citation I have proposed follows that logic by stating the mechanism and not a size. I would add a limit on what we claim from your point. The qualitative result is well supported, but some quantitative implications of the model, such as the size of the productivity gain from reallocation, depend on assumptions like the productivity distribution. The committee should not cite the framework as validated in those respects. I also agree with leaving Redding out. His later work uses the framework for quantitative and spatial analysis, and adding him would broaden the citation toward a different discovery. If the committee decides that crediting the empirical firm-level trade literature is essential, that argues for a different configuration, not for a third name here, and I do not currently favour that.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore prize (B050), citing a clean attribution to one 1997 paper. He concedes that direct identification of the collateral channel is mixed and that the 2022 prize overlaps the adjacent accelerator literature. He also asks whether the 2008 trade prize reduces the appetite for B038.
responses.response: Your two-name attribution for B050 is clean, and on that criterion it matches B038. Our difference is on empirical discipline and on overlap. You say the confirming evidence comes mostly from the adjacent accelerator and intermediary literature, so B050 is supported by evidence that does not test the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism itself. Selection into exporting and reallocation, by contrast, are tested directly on firm-level microdata. On overlap, you and I both apply a distinctness test across prizes: the 2022 prize overlaps with the accelerator side of B050, and the 2008 trade prize is about increasing returns and location. I read the latter as a different discovery from firm selection. On your own standard, the 2022 overlap bears more on B050 than the 2008 overlap bears on B038. I would leave B050 out of my alternatives, but I accept that a committee that values clean attribution above empirical identification could reasonably place it ahead of B015.

responses.point: Fredriksson prefers B036 (Autor, Hanson, Katz). He values its credible quasi-experimental identification and says the boundary question is whether the discovery is one or two. He accepts Dorn in place of Katz as defensible.
responses.response: I agree that B036 has the strongest identification of any labour-market candidate, and I gave it a low opening rank only because of how I judged the construction. Your own boundary question is what keeps it behind B038 for me. If the discovery is the China shock, Dorn belongs and Katz does not. If it is the wider account of technology, tasks and trade, Katz belongs and Dorn does not, and the task lineage runs to Acemoglu and Restrepo outside the credited set. B038 faces a similar question, but the boundary is narrower. The model and its main complements fit in two names, while here the choice of third name changes what is being honoured. The persistence and external validity of the China-shock estimates also remain debated. B036 is not my alternative, but I would not object to it on scientific grounds if you settle the boundary.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have claims strong enough that a two-name Melitz-Helpman citation would be seen as incomplete.
Whether the 2008 trade prize reduces the case for another trade award, and whether the committee applies the same standard to earlier macroeconomics prizes when judging B015.
How much of the welfare-gain implication of the model survives alternative elasticity and productivity-distribution assumptions.
Whether Helpman's credit across other work is correctly accounted for once. I take it as separable from the firm-heterogeneity contribution, but I have not resolved it.
Whether B015's attribution can be settled around a single citation, in which case its influence could outweigh B038's cleaner credit set.
I rely on general knowledge and the supplied round-1 materials and have not independently verified any factual or credit claim.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Melitz, Helpman or Redding, or to the credited names on my alternatives B015 and B001, appears in my supplied profile. I repeat two disclosures. My field of matching, auctions and mechanism design is adjacent to the information-design theory in B001, which was my opening first choice and is now an alternative. I am also an SSE affiliate alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, who comment on B038, B050 and B015. I add that I gave the 2020 presentation speech for the Academy, which may bias me toward applied, implementation-linked work, though it does not establish my preferences. I have not adjudicated any of these ties.
